title: Sable Tech - Private VPC Discovery
summary: Initial technical discovery for Sable Tech's plan to evaluate Redwood Private in a VPC. Covered networking (VPC peering, private endpoints), region constraints, KMS integration, SOC2/ISO questions, and pilot scope. Agreed next steps: send security pack, schedule deep-dive for network team, share pricing for a 3-month pilot.
action_items: Jordan Hayes - send security & compliance pack (SOC2, ISO, KMS integration docs) - due 2027-01-06
Priya Raman - schedule network deep-dive with Sable's infra team and provide VPC diagram template - due 2027-01-04
Dev Patel - share current VPC CIDR ranges and preferred AWS region - due 2027-01-03
next_steps: Redwood to send security pack and onboarding docs
Schedule technical deep dive for week of 2027-01-04
Provide pilot pricing and PVC capacity estimate
Customer to provide VPC CIDRs, preferred region, and compliance checklist
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-30
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 45m
Attendees: Jordan Hayes (Redwood AE), Priya Raman (Redwood SE), Marta Sanchez (Sable Head of Infra), Liam O'Connor (CTO), Dev Patel (Platform Eng)

[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone thanks for joining, um we're excited to talk through how Redwood Private could fit into Sable's infra. quick intro round real fast?
[00:18] Marta: Yeah hi Marta here, I run infra at Sable. we'll mostly be focused on networking and compliance.
[00:26] Liam: Liam - CTO, focused on timelines and cost.
[00:30] Dev: Dev, platform eng, I'll be the one who sets up the VPC peering.
[00:36] Priya: Priya, SE at Redwood - I'll cover the technical pieces and run the deep-dive next week if we need.
[00:42] Jordan: Great, thanks. quick agenda: requirements, network, security, pilot scope, next steps. sound good?
[00:50] Marta: Sounds good.
[01:10] Liam: high level: we need a private deployment, no egress to public internet from model traffic, and keys must be customer-managed. timeline: looking at Q1 pilot.
[01:28] Jordan: cool, when you say no egress are you referring to model weights or inference traffic?
[01:34] Marta: inference traffic - requests and responses must stay inside our VPC or via private endpoints. we also want audit logs forwarded to our SIEM.
[01:44] Priya: okay that lines up with Redwood Private. we support VPC peering and private endpoints (AWS interface endpoints) and can ship audit logs to your S3 or CloudWatch, and we integrate with customer KMS for envelope keys.
[02:02] Dev: can you do VPC peering across accounts and across regions? our infra spans us-east-1 and eu-west-1 but for pilot we'd prefer us-east-1.
[02:12] Priya: VPC peering across accounts is supported. cross-region peering is possible but we usually recommend keeping the Private control plane in the same region as the compute to meet latency and data residency needs. for pilot, us-east-1 is straightforward.
[02:36] Marta: what about private link / interface endpoint option? which one do you recommend?
[02:42] Priya: PrivateLink (interface endpoints) is often preferred for security — you get ENIs in your subnet and no VPC peering route table changes. peering can be simpler in some orgs. both are supported; depends on your network team preference.
[03:00] Dev: what IP ranges do we need to reserve? any chance of overlapping CIDRs causing issues?
[03:06] Priya: We'll provide a recommended list. typically Redwood needs a small set of CIDR ranges for the service ENIs; if there's overlap we can use PrivateLink which uses your ENIs so overlap is less of a problem. we'll also share a VPC diagram template.
[03:22] Liam: KMS — you said can bring your own KMS? do you support AWS KMS CMKs and HSM-backed keys?
[03:30] Priya: Yes, AWS KMS customer-managed keys are supported; for HSM we can integrate with approved HSMs via KMS or external key manager, but we'll need to scope that in the security pack.
[03:44] Marta: SOC2 and ISO certifications — are those in your pack? our procurement requires them.
[03:50] Jordan: yes we'll send SOC2 Type II report and ISO docs and a summary of our compliance posture. also the audit log examples and retention options.
[04:02] Dev: what's the networking flow for inference? is traffic routed to a public endpoint then back or stays internal?
[04:08] Priya: With PrivateLink the request stays on the AWS private network; traffic goes from your VPC via the interface endpoint to our service ENIs in the same region. with peering, traffic routes direct via peered VPC routes. either way we can avoid NAT egress.
[04:30] Liam: region constraints — do you require specific AZs or instance types? we run mixed instance families.
[04:36] Priya: For Redwood Private we support a range of instance types; we recommend GPU-backed instances for model serving. AZ distribution matters for redundancy; for pilot a single AZ is fine but for production we recommend multi-AZ. we'll provide supported instance matrix.
[04:58] Marta: latency SLOs? if we host in us-east-1 what's typical p95?
[05:03] Priya: depends on model and size; for small conversational models p95 token latency can be low 120-200ms within region; we'll include performance profiles per model in the deck. for finetuned or larger models numbers will be higher.
[05:24] Dev: any special firewall or outbound ports? our security team locks down everything.
[05:30] Priya: We'll provide a firewall rules list — typically allow HTTPS on 443 for control plane comms (if you use Private control plane there are private endpoints) and private traffic over the PrivateLink ENIs. No public internet egress required for inference.
[05:52] Jordan: curious on quotas and capacity — what's the smallest reserved commit for Dedicated/Private?
[05:58] Priya: For Dedicated there's monthly commit tiers; for Private deployment pilot we do a short-term reserved pool, often a 3-month pilot with a small GPU pod. we can size by QPS and token throughput — if you share expected concurrency and average prompt size we'll produce a capacity estimate.
[06:20] Liam: for pilot scope we want to validate latency, cost per 1k tokens, and security integration. success criteria would be under 250ms p95 for our target model and keys fully managed by us.
[06:34] Jordan: good criteria. Marta any regulatory constraints for data residency?
[06:39] Marta: We store customer data in-region only; for EU customers we can't leave eu-west. for this pilot it's us-only but that matters for future expansion.
[06:50] Priya: noted — we can support region restrictions. control plane can be private or SaaS; for strict residency we recommend private control plane in your VPC.
[07:02] Dev: about logging — can we push audit logs to our SIEM in near-real time?
[07:08] Priya: yes we have log forwarding to S3/CloudWatch and can set up an event forwarder to your SIEM. latency is typically under a minute depending on config.
[07:20] Liam: any gotchas around VPC peering quotas or route table entries? our cloud quota is tight.
[07:26] Priya: peering requires route table updates; if quotas are tight PrivateLink reduces route table churn but consumes ENI quotas. we'll work with your cloud team on the preferred pattern.
[07:42] Marta: encryption at rest — is model cache encrypted with our keys?
[07:47] Priya: yes the KV cache and persisted artifacts can be encrypted with your CMK; the security pack shows how envelope encryption is used.
[07:58] Dev: can we run a canary model on Redwood Hosted and then failover to Private if needed?
[08:04] Priya: We support rollouts and fallback policies. many customers use hosted for dev and then dedicated/private for prod. fallback requires compatibility between model variants.
[08:18] Jordan: good. any procurement/legal items upfront?
[08:23] Marta: our legal will want data processing addendum and standard security terms.
[08:28] Jordan: we'll include a sample DPA and enterprise terms in the pack.
[08:34] Liam: timeline — if we start pilot in mid-Jan when do you need our VPC info?
[08:40] Priya: ideally a week before onboarding. so if pilot mid-Jan, share CIDRs and region by first week of Jan.
[08:52] Dev: we'll confirm CIDR ranges.
[08:56] Marta: pricing — can you give a rough 3-month pilot cost now?
[09:01] Jordan: rough estimate: depends on instance type and traffic but we'll send a pilot pricing sheet; for planning purpose assume small GPU pod ~ $Xk/month plus support. we'll put exact numbers in the follow-up.
[09:18] Priya: also note cost levers — quantization, batching, and caching can reduce token cost significantly; we'll show recommended config.
[09:34] Liam: security review — can we schedule a 1-hour session with our security operations next week?
[09:39] Jordan: yes we'll set that up; Priya you'll lead the network portion?
[09:44] Priya: Yep I'll lead. I'll bring our network diagram and typical firewall/rules doc.
[09:52] Marta: One more — do you support SSO and RBAC for console?
[09:57] Priya: Yes SAML SSO and role-based access controls are supported. we'll include admin onboarding steps.
[10:08] Dev: anything special for multi-account setups? we run prod/dev in separate accounts.
[10:13] Priya: We support multi-account via cross-account peering or sharing endpoints; the security pack will include patterns.
[10:24] Jordan: okay let's recap next steps.
[10:28] Marta: before that a quick question: what monitoring/tracing hooks do you provide?
[10:33] Priya: We provide per-request tracing headers, per-model metrics in console, token-level cost breakdown and logs; can export traces to your tracing system.
[10:44] Jordan: Recap: Redwood to send security pack (SOC2/ISO, KMS integration docs, DPA), pilot pricing, VPC diagram template. Schedule network deep-dive with Priya and security review with Jordan. Customer to share CIDRs, preferred region (us-east-1), and expected concurrency.
[11:05] Liam: sounds good.
[11:10] Marta: thanks all. we'll aim to get those items to you this week.
[11:16] Jordan: thanks everyone, we'll follow up with calendar invites and the pack.
[11:22] End meeting

Notes on transcript quality: occasional mis-attributions and minor ASR errors (e.g., KMS spoken as 'K M S' in places). References shared: security pack link (placeholder) https://redwood.example.com/sec-pack/sable-tech , VPC diagram template https://redwood.example.com/templates/vpc-diagram.pdf
